candidates.title: ElevenLabs in early talks for funding at $33 billion valuation
candidates.snippet: ElevenLabs in early talks for funding at $33 billion valuation The Economic Times
candidates.text:
Synopsis
The company plans to kick off the efforts in the first three months of 2027, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Discussions are preliminary, though some investors are pushing for the process to start sooner, they said.
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen
Reuters
ElevenLabs , a company building artificial intelligence voice models and agents, is in early discussions for a funding round at a target valuation of $33 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
The company plans to kick off the efforts in the first three months of 2027, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Discussions are preliminary, though some investors are pushing for the process to start sooner, they said.
ElevenLabs’ annual recurring revenue , an estimate of yearly sales calculated from a shorter time period, is now $700 million, one of the people said. In September, the company said its ARR had reached $600 million.
ElevenLabs declined to comment.
The startup was last valued at $22 billion in September after completing an employee tender offer. The company generally announces valuations at a multiple of 11, in reference to its name.
Abiding by that rule would give ElevenLabs an outsize valuation among its broader peer base, even allowing for the wide variation in the way AI companies are valued and measure ARR. London-based video AI startup Synthesia was valued at $4 billion in January, with about $140 million in ARR, according to a February blog post. French model maker Mistral AI was valued at €21 billion in September, hitting an ARR of $400 million in early 2026.
But investors may be spurred on by Anthropic’s record $107.3 billion initial public offering, which delivered huge windfalls for early backers and reinforced hopes that the current crop of highly valued AI firms can deliver huge returns.
ElevenLabs was formed in London by Polish entrepreneurs Mati Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski in 2022, and makes voice and audio models for realistic-sounding synthetic voices that can be used for games, audiobooks and for interactive AI agents.
Chief Executive Officer Staniszewski has previously said the company may start preparing for an IPO in 2028.
The company also recently launched a product that can flag if audio in a live stream is coming from a human or AI.
“Today you assume that you’re interacting with a human unless it’s proven to be AI,” Staniszewski said in a previous interview with Bloomberg News. “In the future I think it will be the opposite.”

candidates.title: FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia
candidates.snippet:
FrenchFry Acquisitions has agreed to combine with Tavia Acquisition Corp. in a transaction that values FrenchFry at $500 million. FrenchFry equityholders would receive 45 million shares in the combined company, valued at $10 per share for the transaction, plus $50 million in convertible promissory notes.
The post FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:20 AM
FrenchFry Sets $500 Million Enterprise Value In Deal To Go Public With Tavia
FrenchFry Acquisitions has agreed to combine with Tavia Acquisition Corp. in a transaction that values FrenchFry at $500 million. FrenchFry equityholders would receive 45 million shares in the combined company, valued at $10 per share for the transaction, plus $50 million in convertible promissory notes.
Two Businesses Built Around Shared AI Tools
The combined company would operate as FrenchFry Holdings and seek a Nasdaq listing. At closing, it would own FrenchFry AI, a no-code platform that helps sales teams find and contact prospective customers, and Catalyst Holdings, which has developed tools for launching and growing apps and games.
Catalyst plans to fund apps and games in exchange for a share of revenue. FrenchFry also plans to acquire established businesses where it sees opportunities to automate manual sales, marketing or customer service work. The holding company intends to provide its businesses with shared finance, accounting, legal and human resources functions.
FrenchFry AI has generated minimal revenue to date, and Catalyst has yet to make an investment or generate revenue, according to the announcement. The combined company expects to need additional capital to pursue its acquisition and investment plans.
The parties expect the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Tavia shareholder approval, an effective registration statement, Nasdaq listing approval and other closing conditions.
KEY QUOTE
“This is a significant milestone toward completing our business combination with FrenchFry. FrenchFry Holdings is built on one AI layer serving many growth businesses. We believe there are thousands of small to medium-sized companies that can benefit from this platform. As a public company, FrenchFry Holdings expects to have the access to capital it needs to grow FrenchFry.ai and to make Catalyst’s first investments and acquisitions, which can run on its AI agents with minimal added overhead.”
Andy Wiederhorn, Executive Chairman And Chief Executive Officer Of Tavia Acquisition Corp.

candidates.snippet: Tempus AI Secures $385M Term Loan Facility to Fund Personalis Deal Unite.AI
candidates.text:
Funding
Tempus AI Secures $385M Term Loan Facility to Fund Personalis Deal
Published
November 25, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
AI-generated illustration
Key Points Tempus secured $385 million in term loans and $115 million revolving to help fund the…
View more
Tempus secured $385 million in term loans and $115 million revolving to help fund the Personalis acquisition.
The deal pays Personalis holders roughly $600 million cash and $900 million in Tempus Class A stock.
Borrowing remains contingent on the acquisition closing or being reasonably expected to close within one business day.
Tempus AI entered a senior secured credit agreement on November 25, 2026, providing $385 million of term-loan commitments and $115 million of revolving commitments to help finance its pending Personalis acquisition, according to its Form 8-K .
In a separate November 24, 2026 decision, Tempus elected to pay approximately $600 million in cash and issue approximately $900 million in Tempus Class A common stock to Personalis shareholders. These are financing commitments, not evidence that the full amounts have already been drawn. Initial funding requires the acquisition to have closed or be reasonably expected to close within one business day after funding.
Debt Terms and Funding Conditions
Tempus expects borrowings to fund part of the acquisition consideration and related transaction costs, as well as working capital and general corporate purposes. Ares Capital Corporation is the administrative and collateral agent, Ares Capital Management LLC the lead arranger and bookrunner, and ACF Finco I LP the revolving agent.
Term loans bear interest at either the agreement’s Base Rate benchmark plus 4.50% or its Term SOFR benchmark plus 5.50%; revolving loans use Base Rate plus 2.75% or Term SOFR plus 3.75%. Term SOFR has a 1.00% floor, the Base Rate a 2.00% floor, and interest on the loans is payable solely in cash.
Both facilities mature on the fifth anniversary of the effective date. A springing provision can move maturity to 91 days before Tempus’s 0.75% convertible senior notes due 2030 unless those notes are repaid or converted first or specified liquidity requirements are met.
Certain Tempus subsidiaries will guarantee the obligations, which are secured by substantially all assets of Tempus and those subsidiaries. The agreement includes minimum-liquidity and minimum-revenue covenants. Revolving availability depends on eligible accounts receivable and certain qualified cash, subject to reserves and other limitations, and revolving interest can be charged on a minimum balance even when actual borrowings are lower.
Revised Acquisition Consideration
The cash election uses flexibility described in Tempus’s July 20, 2026 acquisition announcement . The merger agreement priced Personalis at $16.25 per common share, representing approximately $1.5 billion in enterprise value net of Tempus’s existing ownership. Consideration was originally structured as all stock, with Tempus holding an option to pay cash capped at 50% of the consideration and a floating exchange ratio capped at 0.3356 Tempus shares per Personalis share.
The cash estimate assumes 108,740,631 Personalis shares outstanding immediately before closing and no perfected appraisal demands. The number of shares designated for cash can automatically decrease, with a corresponding increase in the stock portion, to satisfy the merger agreement’s reorganization threshold, determined using Tempus’s closing-date trading price.
AI-Enabled Oncology Rationale
Tempus says the acquisition pairs its multimodal data, AI capabilities and commercial infrastructure with Personalis’s tumor-informed molecular residual disease (MRD) technology, including the NeXT Personal test, which detects small traces of circulating tumor DNA to monitor treatment response, residual cancer and recurrence.
The transaction builds on a partnership established in November 2023, through which Tempus invested in Personalis and commercialized NeXT Personal. Tempus CEO Eric Lefkofsky called MRD “a large and rapidly growing market” and said the collaboration had demonstrated the strength of combining Personalis’s technology with his company’s commercial infrastructure.
Tempus originally expected the acquisition to close in late 2026 or early 2027. Closing remains subject to Personalis stockholder adoption of the merger agreement and other customary conditions. Tempus has now aligned the debt package with its cash-and-stock election, but the borrowing timetable and the proposed AI-supported MRD expansion both remain tied to completion of the acquisition.

candidates.title: Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan
candidates.snippet:
Vena Energy has secured a $113 million green loan from BNP Paribas and Standard Chartered to refinance five operating wind and solar projects in Indonesia. The facility provides fixed-rate financing with maturities of up to 17.5 years for assets with a combined generating capacity of 114 megawatts.
The post Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:31 PM
Vena Energy Locks In Long-Term Fixed Rates For Five Indonesian Projects With $113 Million Green Loan
Vena Energy has secured a $113 million green loan from BNP Paribas and Standard Chartered to refinance five operating wind and solar projects in Indonesia. The facility provides fixed-rate financing with maturities of up to 17.5 years for assets with a combined generating capacity of 114 megawatts.
Wind And Solar Assets Covered By The Refinancing
The portfolio includes the 72-megawatt Tolo Wind Project in South Sulawesi and four solar projects in North Sulawesi and West Nusa Tenggara. Together, the solar projects account for the remaining 42 megawatts. The refinancing gives the operating projects a long-term funding base and makes interest costs more predictable over the life of the loans.
Both banks served as arrangers, hedge counterparties and green loan coordinators. BNP Paribas also acted as facility agent, while Standard Chartered served as account bank.
Vena Energy, the renewable energy arm of Vena Group, has operated in Indonesia since 2019. The company says its local projects support employment, skills development and opportunities for nearby businesses. Across the Asia-Pacific region, Vena Energy reported a 30.5-gigawatt development pipeline as of December 31, 2025, spanning onshore wind, solar and offshore wind.
KEY QUOTE
“This refinancing reflects the strength of Vena Energy’s Indonesian operating portfolio and our ability to optimise the capital structure of established renewable energy assets. By securing long-term financing, we are strengthening the financial position of our portfolio while maintaining a stable funding base for these assets. We value the continued support of BNP Paribas and Standard Chartered, which reflects confidence in the quality of our projects and their long-term performance.”
Ravi Nichani, Co-Head Of Investment At Vena Group

candidates.title: Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility
candidates.snippet:
Blulabs has closed an $80 million asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo, including a $20 million accordion feature. The multiyear facility is secured by receivables and inventory and replaces the supply chain company’s previous trade-finance and factoring arrangements.
The post Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:52 AM
Blulabs Moves To Bank-Backed Financing With An $80 Million Wells Fargo Facility
Blulabs has closed an $80 million asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo, including a $20 million accordion feature. The multiyear facility is secured by receivables and inventory and replaces the supply chain company’s previous trade-finance and factoring arrangements.
Blulabs plans to use the facility to support working capital, inventory and the expansion of customer programs. It serves airlines, hospitality businesses, distributors and retailers through a global manufacturing and logistics network. The company is also developing software to give its teams real-time visibility into purchase orders, production schedules, freight routing and inventory.
The financing follows a May 2026 investment led by Lodestone Capital at a $160 million pre-money valuation. Blulabs intends to redeem that investment in spring 2027, which would return full ownership to the Garson family.
KEY QUOTES
“Moving to an institutional banking partner like Wells Fargo is a milestone for Blulabs and for our family. It reflects the scale and discipline of the company, and it shows the market that Blulabs is built for whatever the next 20 years of the supply chain have in store. Our vision is a Blulabs product in every hand, so that it’s impossible to go out into the world without interacting with something we’ve made, moved or delivered.”
Cole Garson, Co-CEO Of Blulabs
“Under the leadership of Marc Garson and his family, Blulabs has grown their supply solutions to serve many leading brands. We are pleased to support Blulabs with a flexible capital solution as the company continues to serve its customers and scale its global platform.”
Rich Schultz, Managing Director At Wells Fargo Capital Finance
“This business has always been about trust. Customers trust us because we solve problems, keep our commitments and stand behind them when markets are difficult. Having Wells Fargo behind us is a recognition of what this family has built, and it gives the next generation the strength to take Blulabs to its next level. As the father and founder of this company, I could not be more proud of this milestone.”
Marc Garson, Founder And Chairman Of Blulabs
“AI is changing how the physical economy works, and we are at the frontier in our market. Pairing that technology with the capital strength of this facility will transform Blulabs in ways that are hard to comprehend through today’s lens. In a short time, we will deliver for our customers at a scale that wasn’t conceivable before.”
Remy Garson, Co-CEO Of Blulabs

Mumbai leads in company count while Gurugram secures majority funding in India's protein ecosystem.

India’s protein-focused companies raised $46 million in equity funding across 12 rounds on a year-to-date basis, according to a report by Tracxn. Funding in the sector stood at $48 million in the full year 2025 and $15 million in 2024.
The ecosystem has raised $679 million in total equity funding, with 67 of the 392 companies having secured funding. Of these, 51 companies have raised equity funding, while 10 have progressed to Series A or later, including five companies that have raised Series B or later.

Funding activity remained relatively subdued in 2026, with the total number of rounds falling to 12, compared with 28 in 2025 and 16 in 2024. Most of the capital raised this year went into two late-stage rounds, while no early-stage rounds were recorded. Seed-stage activity continued, albeit at a smaller scale.
Gurugram leads funding, Mumbai tops company count
Gurugram accounted for 52% of the ecosystem’s total funding, largely driven by Bright LifeCare and Absolute, which have raised $382 million and $116 million, respectively. Together, the two companies account for a significant share of the capital raised by the sector.
Mumbai followed with 15% of total funding, with companies such as The Whole Truth Foods, SuperYou and Phab among the notable funded players. Bengaluru accounted for around 6% of funding, led by companies including Yoga Bar, Loopworm and Phyx44.

candidates.text:
Other 25.11.2026
Back to news
Over £45 million in funding from the Creative Industries Sector Plan will benefit the gaming industry
Image credit: Unsplash via Nathaniel Cherian
A consortium of eight gaming studios is set to benefit from a government disbursement exceeding £45 million, which is aimed at bolstering various creative industries. This is part of UK Research and Innovation's (UKRI) substantial £500 million allocation under the Creative Industries Sector Plan.
Among the studios selected for the Next Wave Pilot initiative, facilitated by Innovate UK, are Huey Games and Ten24 Media. This program supports 40 small to medium-sized businesses in the creative technology sector with a cumulative £10 million investment.
The funding recipients include AUXA, Digital Tactics, Giggle Byte Studios, Locat Technology, Lurtis, and Parable Studios. They will each receive financial backing for projects valued between £110,000 and £500,000, with an obligation for companies to cover at least 30% of project costs.
Rob Hewson, CEO and creative director of Huey Games, stated, "AI is poised to transform game development, and this presents a leadership opportunity for Britain." He noted that Innovate UK's Breakthrough Wave provides the necessary support for Huey Games to develop AI tools for global studios, with work being conducted from Manchester by an all-UK team.
The financial package includes an additional £34 million aimed at establishing a second batch of five creative industry clusters, along with £2.2 million dedicated to the Great North Creative Corridor and £5 million to prolong the Creative Industries Policy and Evidence Centre.
Professor Christopher Smith, Creative Industries Champion at UKRI, remarked, "The newly announced investments in our leading creative industries are both ambitious and comprehensive. They range from five new Creative Industries Clusters across the UK to 40 pioneering businesses in createch." He emphasized the crucial role these investments play in the UK's future economic landscape through innovation and creativity.
Moreover, earlier this year, the UK Games Fund revealed its largest funding round since its inception in 2015, supporting 29 independent studios with grants up to £100,000 via an enlarged Prototype Fund.

candidates.text:
Agricultural Technology
IoT

Myriota secures USD $40 million in Series C funding
Wed, 25th Nov 2026
KAREN JOY BACUDO
Finance Editor
Myriota has secured the first USD $40 million tranche of its Series C funding round, led by existing investors Main Sequence Ventures and the National Reconstruction Fund Corporation.
The Adelaide-based satellite internet of things company completed the first close in 100 days, taking total funding to more than USD $107.5 million. Hostplus also participated in the round, while Funds SA joined as a new investor.
The funding will support expansion into new industrial sectors and international markets, and help build out Myriota's satellite infrastructure, including development and launch work for a next generation of satellites.
Myriota operates in industrial internet of things markets where customers need to track and monitor assets in remote areas. Its platform is used in applications including mining equipment, shipping containers, fuel tanks, livestock water supplies and off-grid solar systems.
It provides services directly in 57 markets and has teams across 19 locations globally.
Expansion plans
Over the past year, Myriota has added two products to its platform: HyperPulse, a 5G non-terrestrial network and terrestrial service, and AssetHawk, a tracker for industrial assets. It has also expanded further into industrial fuels, with fuel tank monitoring deployments growing across North America and Latin America.
The latest funding comes as the company scales up its satellite network. Myriota launched 16 satellites in 2026 and has further launches booked for 2027 and 2028.
A larger constellation would give customers more network redundancy and greater service capacity for larger deployments. Myriota focuses on narrowband communications for industrial users operating beyond the reach of conventional terrestrial networks.
Ben Cade, Chief Executive Officer of Myriota, said the investment would support the company's next phase of growth.
"We're at the beginning of a fundamental shift in industrial IoT. Industries increasingly rely on data from the field to make decisions about their operations, assets and resources, and as AI moves into the physical world, that data becomes even more essential. Myriota is building the infrastructure to connect the physical world at unprecedented scale. Bringing forward the first close of our Series C reflects the strong confidence of our investors and enables us to accelerate our growth, expand into new markets and advance our technology. It also marks an important phase for Australia's defence industrial base, as Myriota consolidates its position as a true tier 1, global telco delivering secure, narrowband IoT communications from space," Cade said.
Investor backing
The National Reconstruction Fund Corporation had previously backed Myriota as part of its investment activity in the space sector. The company's origins lie in research at the University of South Australia.
"Myriota was one of the NRFC's earliest space sector investments, and its innovative technology was developed from research at UniSA. It is a powerful example of how space-enabled technologies play a key role in solving real-world challenges right here on Earth. Myriota's satellite-based industrial IoT provides critical, field-based intelligence for sectors operating in remote areas such as agriculture, utilities, logistics, mining, environmental monitoring and defence, and our decision to invest further in this company is a testament to its potential to grow into a global, space-based Australian telecommunications company," said David Gall, Chief Executive Officer of NRFC.
Main Sequence Ventures, which first invested in Myriota in 2018, said the company had reached a broader commercial stage for its technology.
"We first backed Myriota in 2018, and it was one of the first companies we helped grow. We believe strongly in the technology. Ultra-low-power satellite communications is unique, and it's now moving into wide use, from tracking shipping containers and mining equipment to monitoring fuel tanks and water supplies. Myriota delivers service directly in 57 markets, which makes it Australia's largest telco by geographic coverage. We're proud to lead this round and to keep backing Ben and the team," said Duursma.
Funds SA said the business was an example of South Australian technology with international reach.
"Homegrown innovation and technology will play an increasingly important role in supporting the businesses and industries that underpin Australia's economy. candidates.title: SMEDAN Announces $25 Million Funding Plan for Nigerians in Agriculture — See Who Can Benefit
candidates.snippet: SMEDAN Announces $25 Million Funding Plan for Nigerians in Agriculture — See Who Can Benefit Nigeria Startup News
candidates.text:
Advertisement
Kindly share this story:
Share
The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) is working with the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA) to unlock at least $25 million in financing for Nigerian agricultural businesses.
Follow us on Google News
The initiative is being implemented in partnership with Kaduna Business School (KBS) and the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC) of Pan-Atlantic University to help agricultural entrepreneurs expand their operations.
Details of the funding plan were disclosed during an agribusiness meeting held in Ibadan, Oyo State, where stakeholders discussed challenges facing businesses in the agricultural sector.
Advertisement
Speaking on behalf of AGRA Nigeria Country Director, Rufus Idris, Dr Godswill Aguiyi said many agricultural enterprises struggled to obtain financing because of inadequate business records and poor financial management.
He disclosed that AGRA had committed an initial $100,000 to a separate facility designed to reduce the cost of professional business support services for agricultural entrepreneurs.
The facility will bring together government agencies, financial institutions and development partners to help businesses access services that could improve their chances of obtaining financing.
The broader programme seeks to connect agricultural enterprises with lenders and investors, alongside providing business training and opportunities to participate in investment pitch competitions.
The support is also intended to help farmers identify reliable buyers, understand market demands and improve the commercial performance of their existing businesses.
The initiative, which commenced on July 1, 2025, is scheduled to run until March 31, 2028.
Who can benefit
According to the official project information published by KBS, agricultural Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and smallholder farmers are among the intended beneficiaries.
Priority will be given to businesses owned or managed by women and young people operating across agricultural value chains.
The project initially focused on Kaduna, Niger and Nasarawa states, while Oyo has also joined AGRA’s focus states.
SMEDAN had previously disclosed plans to promote the inclusion of women and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in the programme.
Meanwhile, Aguiyi revealed that more than 10,000 young Nigerians applied for a recent agricultural innovation competition conducted under the initiative.
Ten successful entrepreneurs received a combined ₦17 million to develop their businesses following a competitive selection process.
How to benefit
Interested agricultural entrepreneurs can visit the official project page at https://kbs.edu.ng/collaborations/agra-kbs-project/overview to obtain information about the programme and available support opportunities.
They can also follow announcements from SMEDAN through https://smedan.gov.ng/ for upcoming activities and funding opportunities under the partnership.
Prospective beneficiaries should prepare their business records, financial statements and business plans to improve their readiness for engagement with potential lenders and investors.
The $25 million represents the financing target of the project, rather than an approved cash grant for individual applicants. A dedicated funding application portal and deadline have not been announced.

Sydney estate planning startup Safewill has raised $15 million in a Series C at a $160 million valuation.
Existing backers King River and Reinventure co-led that round, closed a year earlier than planned. Carthona Capital and Flying Fox Ventures also returned, with Admiralty Capital Group, Zip cofounder Larry Diamond, and Betashares cofounders Alex Vynokur and Ilan Israelstam also joining the cap table.
The cash will help acquire more super funds, banks and insurers as customers offering estate planning to their clients. The fintech also plans to automate some of the paperwork families face when settling an estate.
CEO Adam Lubofsky and cofounder Dan Bennett (who’s now left the business) launched Safewill in 2019 to help Australians write a will online. By the time it raised a $17 million Series B in November 2024 , more than 150,000 Australians had written a will on the platform. Safewill raised $3 million in 2021 and another $5.5 million in a Series A extension in 2023.
Deals with Aware Super, UniSuper and Colonial First State (CFS) now give more than five million super fund members access to Safewill.
“Superannuation funds spend decades helping members accumulate wealth and prepare for retirement,” Lubofsky said.

JBWere estimated in 2024 that Australians would inherit $5.4 trillion over the next two decades. Lubofsky said the next opportunity for Safewill is helping the people left to sort out those estates once someone dies.
“While a will creates a legal framework for how an estate should be divided, the difficult part comes when loved ones are left navigating a maze of financial institutions, paperwork and administrative processes to make that happen,” he said.
Reinventure’s Danny Gilligan said Safewill is creating the tech infrastructure for an historically underserved category of financial services.
“What makes the business particularly compelling is the combination of its consumer scale, deepening relationships with Australia’s leading financial institutions, and a team that understands the importance of putting people at the centre of what is ultimately an incredibly personal experience,” he said.
“We believe Safewill has the opportunity to become the defining platform for estate planning and administration in Australia.”

candidates.text:
SA’s Community Wolf raises seed funding round led by Terra Industries
0
By
Tom Jackson
on
November 26, 2026
News , Southern Africa , West Africa
South African public safety tech startup Community Wolf has opened its seed round with a strategic investment from Terra Industries, which takes the strategic lead.
Founded in 2024 by Nick Mills and Michael Houghton, Community Wolf started with a WhatsApp number that lets anyone report crime and suspicious activity for free, anonymously and in their first language.
Its AI models structure the images, video and pin drops users submit, then alert people nearby and local responders. The startup – recently a winner at the South African Startup Awards – has since added emergency assistance, family safety, community communication and operational software for security operators. It has more than 700,000 users and has recorded over 180,000 incidents.
Terra Industries , also founded in 2024, builds autonomous security systems to protect critical infrastructure such as mines, power plants and pipelines across Africa and the Global South. Its air, land and maritime systems run on ArtemisOS, its software platform for large-scale security operations. Disrupt Africa reported in August the company had raised an additional US$18 million in strategic funding to close its own seed round at US$52 million.
The investment in CommunityWolf, the amount of which is undisclosed, marks Terra’s entry into public safety, with Terra CEO Nathan Nwachuku joining Community Wolf’s board. Community Wolf will use the funding to expand into communities around critical and urban infrastructure, while the two companies will also look at linking Community Wolf’s products to Terra’s software, so verified incidents reach Terra’s command centres alongside drone and sensor data.
“The people living around critical assets like mines are the first to feel an attack, and they are often the first to see it coming,” said Nwachuku. “We believe communal security will also be pivotal in how we protect lives and secure infrastructure.”
“Community Wolf gives residents a way to report and security operators an integrated platform to manage their communication and response,” said Mills. “Alongside Terra’s autonomous ground and aerial systems, we can keep millions more people safe across the continent.”

Lawvek Raises Pre-Seed Funding to Help Enterprises Recover Vendor Dues
Lawvek raises $550,000 in a pre-seed round led by Neon Fund to expand its AI platform for identifying vendor overcharges, missed rebates and service credits.
SMEStreet Edit Desk
25 Nov 2026
15:22
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Listen to this article
0.75x 1x 1.5x
00:00 / 00:00
Lawvek, an AI platform that helps enterprises recover vendor overcharges and claim missed rebates and service credits, has raised $550,000 in a pre-seed round led by Neon Fund with participation from Inzas Ventures. The company will use the funding to expand its enterprise customer base and strengthen the platform’s ability to identify and recover money vendors owe.
Co-founders Amrit Khandelwal and Sudip Chhatui started with a problem that cuts across industries. Enterprises negotiate prices, discounts and service commitments with vendors, but the information they need to check whether vendors have honored those terms is often spread across contracts, invoices, usage data and service records.
McKinsey estimates that unmet supplier commitments can cost large enterprises roughly 2% of their spending. For an enterprise with $1 billion in annual spend, that would amount to about $20 million a year.
Lawvek already helps U.S. enterprises identify where they overpay vendors or receive less than they paid for. Its AI agents compare contract terms with billing, usage and service records to flag price increases that exceed agreed caps, volume discounts missing from invoices, and prepaid capacity that teams are on track to leave unused. When a vendor owes a rebate or service credit, Lawvek calculates the amount, gathers the evidence, and files the claim on the customer’s behalf. It then follows up with the vendor and verifies that the credit appears on an invoice or that the customer receives a refund.
“Say a health system negotiates a $2 rebate on every case of exam gloves if its hospitals buy 100,000 cases in a year. As soon as those hospitals reach the threshold, the supplier owes the health system $200,000. Every invoice can be correct, and the health system can still miss the entire rebate,” said Amrit Khandelwal, co-founder and CEO of Lawvek. “Across industries, companies negotiate prices, discounts and service levels, yet still miss overcharges, earned rebates, and credits for outages. Lawvek checks vendors’ bills and performance against their contracts. When a vendor owes money, Lawvek gathers the evidence and follows up until the company receives a credit or refund.”
“The business world is full of blind spots, what’s often referred to as localised ignorance. When we spoke with Lawvek’s customers, we were struck by the scale of the problem and how little
visibility enterprises have into it. We’re pleased to back the team at this early stage as they build and validate the platform with enterprise customers,” said Siddhartha Ahluwalia, partner at Neon Fund.

Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal, and Puneet Sharma, Vegapay provides an issuer processing and credit lifecycle management platform for Credit Line on UPI and credit cards.
Vegapay has raised $10 million in a series A funding round co-led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India and Prosus , with participation from existing investors Elevation Capital and Eximius Ventures.
The Mumbai-based company will deploy the fresh capital to onboard more banks onto credit line on UPI , introduce secured credit lines backed by fixed deposits, gold and mutual funds, expand its credit, prepaid and forex card programmes, and strengthen its engineering and risk teams.

Green Aero raises $14 mn series A funding led by Crane Ventures
The startup will use the capital to expand testing facilities, develop larger-thrust engines, and accelerate flight qualification of autonomous drones and Collaborative Combat Aircraft.
S
Smruthi Nadig
ETEntrepreneur
Published On Nov 26, 2026 at 10:56 AM IST
Share Icon
Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook
Bookmark

Green Aero is developing indigenous propulsion systems and autonomous aircraft, targeting emerging opportunities in aerospace and defence manufacturing.
Green Aero has raised $14 million in a series A funding round led by Crane Ventures , with participation from 3one4 Capital, Antler Elevate, and existing investors pi Ventures , Antler India, and Rebalance.
The capital will support the development of larger-thrust jet engines, flight qualification of transonic and supersonic drones , and the development of autonomous combat aircraft.
Over the next 12 to 18 months, Green Aero plans to expand its engineering team and build larger engine testing facilities, while accelerating the development and flight qualification of its drone platforms. The company is also looking to commercialise its existing jet engines, citing early interest from international buyers.
"The fundraise will generate significant momentum and enable the company to take its initial prototypes through testing and flight qualification for the current demand from the local and global industry for high-speed drones," Dr. Prithwish Kundu, founder and CEO of Green Aero, told ETEntrepreneur .
Founded in November 2023, the company is developing aero engines , autonomous drones and collaborative combat aircraft (CCAs), with an integrated approach spanning propulsion systems, avionics and airframe development.
The company has completed more than 100 hot-fire tests in the sub-kilonewton engine category. It has also developed The Blue Dragon, an aero-engine core built from scratch in India.
The startup’s ecosystem partnerships include L&T, Boeing's BUILD programme and SIDBI's Green-Tech Accelerator.
Its next phase involves developing larger-thrust engines alongside autonomous flight-control systems, edge-computing avionics and navigation capabilities designed to operate in environments where GPS or global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) are unavailable.
Qualification remains a key challenge Despite progress in prototyping, taking indigenous aero engines from development to deployment remains a significant challenge, particularly in a sector where testing, manufacturing precision and flight qualification are critical.
Kundu identified ground and flight qualification of larger engines as some of the biggest challenges facing India's aero-engine ecosystem. He also pointed to precision manufacturing, additive manufacturing and superalloy development as essential capabilities for building competitive propulsion systems.
"Ground and flight qualification of larger engines are some of the key challenges facing the aero-engine ecosystem in India. Precision manufacturing, additive manufacturing and superalloy development are some of the key ingredients for success in this domain," he said.
He added that developing advanced software and edge-computing hardware presented both challenges and opportunities for the sector.
"Development of a world-class software layer and edge computing hardware is another area of challenge as well as opportunity for the ecosystem. We have made significant inroads in these areas and plan to double down on this momentum through R&D, capex investments and skill development," Kundu said.
Green Aero is targeting transonic flight speeds of around 1,000 kmph through its integrated propulsion, avionics and airframe architecture.
"We are massively excited by the vision of building super-fast aircraft and drones in India and for the world. Dr. Prithwish is building a true platform company, across software and hardware to make this vision a reality," said Sidhant Goyal, principal at Crane Ventures.

36Kr Exclusive | A former senior executive of Anker has founded an AI audio equipment startup, which has secured tens of millions of yuan in seed round financing from Boyu Venture Capital and other investors, and its products are about to launch crowdfunding campaigns.
乔钰杰 2026-11-26 10:25
The core of next-generation audio products is the perception and understanding of the live scene.
Writer | QIAO Yujie
Editor | YUAN Silai
This article contains approximately 4,500 words, with an estimated reading time of 11 minutes
36Kr Hard Krypton has learned that HearWell, an AI acoustic perception company, recently completed two rounds of financing totaling tens of millions of yuan, with investments from Boyu Venture Capital, Bright Vision Capital, Plum Ventures, and Xiuyuan Capital, covering both financial investment institutions and industrial investors (institutions are sorted by the alphabetical order of their pinyin initials). Sunward Capital acts as the long-term exclusive financial advisor.
WANG Zhijun, founder of HearWell, previously served as the head of the smart voice recorder business line at iFlytek, and later as the head of the smart audio business at Anker Innovations, where he was responsible for R&D and global sales of audio products such as conference speakerphones and smart speakers. He led the business to achieve a cumulative revenue of over 5 billion yuan in 3 years, launched more than 30 products, and has full-link experience in R&D and commercialization of software and hardware products from 0 to 1 in the field of smart audio devices. After leaving Anker, WANG Zhijun formed a team spanning acoustics, AI algorithms and global commercialization, and founded HearWell.
WANG Zhijun stated that audio technology has gone through stages from "being audible" to "being clear", and then to "being memorable" in the ChatGPT era. The core of the next generation of audio products is the perception and understanding of the scene, a trend that is consistent with the path of AI moving from the digital world to the real world and interacting with the real environment, which is also what he wants to explore and practice by founding HearWell.
Based on this judgment, HearWell takes AI acoustic perception technology as its core. Different from traditional speech-to-text and AI recording summary products, HearWell hopes to start from the sound itself, enabling AI to perceive different sounds in the environment, judge sound events, and understand real scenarios combined with acoustic features such as intonation, speech speed and emotion.
WANG Zhijun summarizes this transformation as moving from Speech to Text to Sound to Understand.
Specifically, the company's technical core is to build an AI acoustic perception platform covering sound collection, acoustic perception, scene understanding and information memory, so that the model can directly understand the sound and the scene where it is located, instead of relying on the intermediate link of speech transcription. At the same time, based on the platformized underlying technical capabilities, the product applications in different scenarios will be gradually expanded, that is, one set of underlying infrastructure can derive multiple products.
Specifically, the technical system of the HearWell acoustic perception application platform mainly includes three levels.
The first is the acoustic collection and processing capability at the physical layer. By simulating the binaural auditory system of the human ear, combined with multi-microphone array, sound source localization and end-side algorithms, the device can identify the direction, distance and type of sound, realize clearer and longer-distance sound collection in complex environments, and retain or filter specific sounds according to user needs. For example, in a noisy coffee shop, the device can focus on retaining the voice of the conversation partner and reduce the interference of surrounding human voices and environmental noise.
The second is the sound event recognition and information extraction capability at the acoustic perception layer. In addition to recognizing speech content, the system also needs to understand the events represented by non-speech sounds. For example, judge the approaching direction of the vehicle through the sound of the car, and identify weather changes combined with environmental sounds such as thunder. Different sounds contain environmental information, and the model needs to identify events from them and judge their possible meanings.
In the scenario of human-to-human communication, this layer mainly solves the problem of accurate recognition. In noisy environments such as coffee shops, surrounding human voices, background music and other sounds are easy to distract attention. Users not only need to separate the voice of the conversation partner from the mixed sounds, but also further identify the specific content expressed by the other party. HearWell hopes to improve the efficiency and accuracy of information reception in complex environments through capabilities such as sound source separation, target sound extraction and speech recognition, and further extract key information in the dialogue to reduce the impact of noise on information understanding and memory.
The third layer is the AI understanding and memory layer. Traditional AI recording products mainly convert sound into text, and then summarize and analyze the text through large models, where tone, emotion and rhythm are "washed away" in this step. HearWell hopes to retrieve these features: introduce original acoustic features such as intonation, speech speed and emotion, combine them with the semantic understanding capability of large models, and restore a more complete communication scenario.
For example, in meetings or face-to-face communications, in addition to recording the specific content of the conversation, the system can also assist in judging the key points and feedb
